correctness.rationale: The affine Artin--Schreier polynomial is irreducible since its pole order m is prime to p, and its y derivative is -1. At infinity the unique local branch z^(m-p)(1-z^(p-1))=x^m has valuation ord(z)=m, ord(x)=m-p. Its generic polar has order m(m-p-1), leaving pm from Bézout. The affine Gauss coordinates u=m*x^(m-1), v=y+m*x^m imply x=dv/du when p does not divide m-1, hence birationality, and become pth powers of birational (x^k,y) coordinates when m=kp+1, hence inseparable degree p. Exact resultants verify small cases, not the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The reduced dual degree is a natural projective invariant of monomial Artin--Schreier plane models and exhibits a sharp, unexpected factor-p dichotomy. The proof separates a fixed polar intersection count pm from a congruence-sensitive Gauss-map degree, exposing geometric inseparability not visible in genus or p-rank; it is a complete natural family classification, not an arbitrary finite sample.
